wa_a_blackstone.blurb: Blackstone is a compact bolted crag on the Little Si side of North Bend, and it is the first wall you meet on the way up the hiking trail. Nine sport lines and one boulder problem share a dark, lichen-streaked face that leans back just a little, with grippy stone and moderate steepness. The sport grades run from 5.6 up through the 5.10s, with the bulk between 5.8 and 5.10, so newer leaders and people stepping up a grade both find something. Routes are a single rope length or a bit shorter, which keeps days here quick and low-key.
wa_a_blackstone.approach: Walk the main Little Si trail uphill, turn left at the marked post, and scramble up the short slope to the base.

wa_central_park.blurb: Central Park is a small outcrop beside Icicle Creek canyon near Leavenworth, holding about ten routes of roughly 50 feet. Protection is a mix of cracks for trad gear and bolts, and the stats show six trad lines to four sport lines. Grades range from 5.7 to 5.10, with most falling at 5.8 and 5.9, which suits climbers working through the moderates. Several lines have anchors you can reach from above for setting up a top rope. From the trail junction the base is only about a minute away.

wa_camp_serene.blurb: Camp Serene is a single big, pale, mossy boulder east of Gold Bar in the Skykomish Valley, with ten problems from V0 up to V8. Most are easy to moderate, V0 to V2, with a couple of V4s, a V6 and a V8 for stronger climbers. Heights make it feel like a highball spot even though there are few lines, and the south face carries the best of them. Logging has cleared the trees that once shaded it, so it now sits open to the sun.
